text:
packet-01 - unverified first image reading (blind). No identification of the work was revealed to me in context.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001.jpg)
- image-001 is a reduced overview of four separate paper leaves laid out 2x2 on black ground, with colour chart and ruler. Modern pencil shelfmark labels visible: top-left "Stams, STA, Frg. 165/2 - 25v"; top-right "... 26v"; bottom-left "... 27v"; bottom-right "... 28v". Small numbered paper tabs at top corners (e.g. "II 20", "II 34").
- Each leaf: single column of long lines, ca. 21-24 lines visible per leaf, written in a fast late-medieval cursive (documentary/notarial type hand, brown ink). Black rectangular masking strips cover the right portion of several lines on each leaf (these hide text; they are part of the imaging, not damage I can read through). Grey squares also mask areas at top right of two leaves. Brown foxing spots throughout; a few binding/sewing holes along the right edge.
- Top-left leaf (25v): line 1-2 appear to be a heading set off ("... ?pro ... / ... "), then an enlarged cursive initial (looks like "V" or "Q"?) opening a new paragraph at line 3. Text looks like legal-procedural prose (compar(uit), ... commissarius ..., publica ..., sigillo ...).
- Top-right leaf (26v): continuous text, then a new paragraph with an enlarged initial (looks like "N"? or "M") near line 13-14 after "et est talis" (which ends short line 12).
- Bottom-left (27v) and bottom-right (28v): continuous prose, no enlarged initials visible at this scale; several words underlined/struck? (a line under "... Citatorum ..." on 28v).
- Interpretation (tentative): a notarial instrument or court-procedure record (citations, commissary judge, sealed letters). Not inferring further.
- Tiles image-002..005 are presumably native-resolution quadrants of this overview; pattern repeats for later overviews.
